sounds.intro: Farsi has no articles and no gender. Learn these sounds and you can read the Latin spelling.
rows: throaty, like French "r", also like a gargling g

phrases.title: Formal and informal
phrases.note: to (informal): friends, family, children. shomaa (formal): strangers, elders, shops. shomaa is also the plural "you". Verb endings change too (-i with to, -id with shomaa). Tarof is a polite style: you may refuse a gift once or twice before accepting.

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Farsi has no gender: "u" means he, she or it. shomaa is polite "you" and plural "you".

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Add -haa to most nouns (ketaab → ketaabhaa). For people, -aan is used too (daaneshjoo → daaneshjooyaan). After a number the noun stays singular: se ketaab.

grammar.title: Regular verbs (present tense)
text: mi- + stem + personal ending. Endings: -am, -i, -ad (-e), -im, -id, -and. Khordan (to eat), stem khor:

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: Word order is subject, object, verb (verb last). Adjectives come after the noun with -e: khaane-ye bozorg.
ex: we live in a big house
maa dar khaane-ye bozorg zendegi mikonim
maa dar khaa-neh-YE bo-ZORG zen-de-GEE mee-ko-NEEM
ما در خانه بزرگ زندگی می‌کنیم

grammar.title: Negation
text: Put na- (or ne- before mi-) before the verb. nemikhoram = I do not eat. Negative words go with the negative verb: hichi nemikhaam.
Add ne- before the verb (before mi- in the present): nemikhaam (I do not want). Double negatives are normal. nist / nistam = is not / am not.
ex: I do not have a car
he does not work on Sundays

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Farsi has no question-word for yes / no. Raise your voice at the end, or begin with aayaa (formal).

grammar.title: Possessives
text: Add the ending to the noun: ketaab-am (my book). Endings: -am, -at, -esh, -emoon, -etoon, -eshoon.

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: to / -i with friends, family. shomaa / -id with strangers and elders. Add aagha (Mr) or khaanom (Ms) before a name, or "jaan" (dear) after a close friend's name.

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Past: stem + -d / -t + ending (-am, -i, -, -im, -id, -and), no mi-. Future: khaahad + short infinitive; in speech the present is often used.

grammar.title: Commands
text: Informal: be- + stem (befarmaa = please do). boro! (go), biyaa! (come). Plural / polite: add -id (biyaayid). Negative: na- + stem (naro, naayaa).

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: tavaanestan = can (mitoonam), baayad = must (baayad beram), khaastan = want (mikhaam beram). Cannot = nemitoonam. Must not = nabaayad.
ex: I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: dar = in / at; roo-ye = on; zir-e = under; kenaar-e = next to; nazdik-e = near. Use -e (ezafe) after the place word: roo-ye miz.
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the table
the shop is next to the bank
the park is near the station
the key is in the bag

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: Add -tar to the adjective (bozorg-tar = bigger) and az for "than". The most = -tarin (bozorg-tarin). khub, behtar, behtarin = good, better, best.
